brief.headline: Wealth Management Invest: Expanding Access to Private Markets with Blackstone’s Farhad Karim
bullets: Family Offices & Wealth: Blackstone Private Wealth’s Farhad Karim details how evergreen funds and semiliquid investment structures are leading to the growing adoption of alternative investments among financial advisors.
Fundraising: Private markets firm KKR raised $25bn (£18.5bn) of new capital in the third quarter, with $14bn coming from its credit and liquid strategies business.

Earnings & AUM: KKR posted growing quarterly profit and record fee-related earnings during the third quarter of 2026 as the private equity giant stepped up asset sales and returned capital to investors, despite a challenging environment due to elevated interest rates.
Real Estate: Australian land lease operator Ingenia Communities Group has readmitted Warburg Pincus to its data room after the US private equity firm raised its takeover offer for a fourth time.
Fundraising: Elikonos Capital has completed the final close of its third private equity fund, Elikonos 3 S.C.A.
brief.marketRead: Bottom line: signals are mixed, with some markets calm and others showing strain, so expect selective risk-taking. The S&P 500 stands at 7,353.73 (down 4.4% on the prior reading) and the VIX is 28.2, an elevated reading that signals nervous markets. The effective fed funds rate is 3.88%, the 10-year Treasury yield is 4.84% (down 6 bps on the prior reading) and the 10Y–2Y yield curve is +0.35 pts (positively sloped). High-yield credit spreads are 3.42%, near long-run norms (down 6 bps on the prior reading).

items.takeaway: Rising prices point to the Fed increasing borrowing costs before Christmas.

items.title: KKR pulls in $25bn in Q3 as credit leads the way
items.takeaway: Private markets firm KKR raised $25bn (£18.5bn) of new capital in the third quarter, with $14bn coming from its credit and liquid strategies business.
items.whyItMatters: KKR pulling in $25bn shows demand for private markets is still growing, and money keeps flowing to the biggest managers, which gives them more say over fees and terms.
items.marketContext: The S&P 500 stands at 7,353.73 (down 4.4% on the prior reading) and the 10-year Treasury yield is 4.84% (down 6 bps on the prior reading). Stock and bond levels change how much room investors have for private assets. When public holdings fall, private allocations look overweight (the "denominator effect"). (FRED data as of Nov 6.)

beginnerNote.explanation: The total market value of money a firm invests on behalf of clients. It is the main yardstick of an asset manager's size.

items.title: TPG-backed Yoco secures $100m private credit facility from Victory Park
items.takeaway: South African fintech company Yoco Technologies, backed by private equity firm TPG, has secured a $100m private credit facility from Victory Park Capital Advisors to expand financing for small businesses, according to a report by Bloomberg.
items.whyItMatters: TPG's $100m deal shows private lenders are still putting money to work in private credit, and the terms they win set the bar for returns across the strategy.
items.marketContext: The effective fed funds rate is 3.88% and high-yield credit spreads are 3.42%, near long-run norms (down 6 bps on the prior reading). Most private loans pay a floating rate, so lender income tracks short-term rates while spreads show how much extra investors demand for credit risk. (FRED data as of Nov 6.)

beginnerNote.explanation: Loans made by investment funds rather than banks, usually to mid-sized companies. They often pay higher, floating interest rates.
